newsitem.title: USA: Most US debt futures flat, sit near four-mos highs.
newsitem.headline: Most US debt futures flat, sit near four-mos highs.

text.p: Most U.S. debt futures were unchanged, sitting near four-month highs after U.S. data this week showed continued U.S. growth with few inflationary pressures, traders and analysts said.
"This market has been fairly bullet-proof all week," one T-bond futures analyst said. "And it just accents what a strong market we have."

September T-bonds traded to 112-08/32, near the four-month high of 112-13/32, in early trade after surviving a sell-off on Thursday that pushed it 111-26/32. The contract posted a double-bottom at 111-17/32 on Wednesday and Tuesday.
Traders said technicians and some locals have tried to sell the market on any dips, hoping to generate downside momentum. However, sellers have emerged with marginal gains to huge losses, they said.
"The end-user in this market has been a buyer, not a seller," another floor analyst said.
The bullish tone in the market was strengthened by this week's U.S. economic data which suggested that the Federal Reserve will not tighten U.S. rates at their July 1-2 meeting.
"There is a 50-50 chance of a tightening in August," one bond trader said about the Fed's August 19 policy meeting.

He said the market was still clinging to expectations of a rate hike later in the summer, judging from where the September Fed funds were trading. The contract was pricing in a Fed funds rate of more than 5.60 percent.
Eurodollars were hemmed into narrow ranges, with December trading between 93.95 and 93.94 on light local activity. Some retail buying was noted at the opening, a floor source said.

December is expected to hold support at 93.92, but is seen rising no higher than 94.00 in the intermediate term, traders said. December rose near 94.00 on Friday, June 13, but last traded above that level in late February 1997.
One bond trader said the Group of Seven (G7) summit that begins today in Denver could sway price action.
But given the absence of news on Friday, expiration of July T-bond options at midday could be the one feature driving the market before midday, traders said.
Several traders said September T-bonds could gravitate to the 112-00 level, as the number of outstanding July options on futures contracts is concentrated in July 112-00 calls.
"You've got triple the number of calls against July 112-00 puts," one bond trader said.

At the close, September T-bonds were up 02/32 at 112-08/32, December Eurodollars were steady at 93.95, and 10-year notes were also unchanged at 108-18/32. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
